question: Why does spec 0018 say to read a pair's `distribution` and never its `summary` when asking how the five reruns split, given that spec 0017 requires every verdict to carry a count like '5 of 5 succeeded'?

items.text: **AC-4**: A pair tagged `stability-probe` is judged differently, but only once AC-3's own 3 of 5 successes floor is met (fewer than 3 successes is still `inconclusive` under AC-3, unchanged). With 3 or more successes, `expectedBand` is not consulted and no majority is computed: the pair passes only if every one of its successful reruns' band is inside `acceptableBands`. One success landing outside that set fails the pair even if every other success matched, since this pair's whole point is that no single run should be trusted as the answer. Because there may be no single winning band, this pair's verdict is always reported as its observed distribution (e.g. `{ strong_match: 3, possible_match: 2 }`), never a lone band.

The report's `summary` field reads like `"possible_match, 5 of 5 succeeded"`, and the `5 of 5` there is the **success denominator**, meaning all five reruns returned a band rather than failing. It is not the count landing on that band.

**AC-6**: Every printed and reported verdict names its own denominator (e.g. "good_match, 3 of 3 succeeded" or, for a distribution shaped verdict, "3 strong_match / 2 possible_match, 5 of 5 succeeded"), never just a band on its own,

A pair's verdict needs at least 3 of its 5 reruns to be scored successes; with fewer than 3, the pair is `inconclusive` (sub reason `insufficient-successes`), reporting whatever successes did land, never silently folded into a pass or a fail. With 3 or more successes, and the pair is not tagged `stability-probe` (AC-4 covers that case separately): compute how many of the successes landed on each band. If one band holds a strict majority (more than half of the successes), that is the pair's verdict band, and the pair passes if that band equals `expectedBand`, or, when `acceptableBands` is present, if it is one of them. If no band holds a strict majority (e.g. a 2 and 2 split out of 4 successes, or a 1, 1, 1 split out of 3), the pair is `inconclusive` (sub reason `no-majority`) UNLESS `acceptableBands` is present and every successful rerun's band is inside it, in which case the pair passes with no single verdict band, reporting the full observed split instead
Read `distribution`, never `summary`, when the question is how the reruns split.

**AC-2**: Every pair is scored through the real `scoreListing()` path, passing the run's one minted fixture session (`session.jar`) as its `cookieAdapter` argument, exactly the shape `test/integration/fit-scoring-live.test.ts` already uses. One session is minted once for the whole run (not once per pair), reused by every call. A pair's five reruns happen one after another inside that pair's own test body (never fired at once), because they exist to measure how much the same input moves between separate calls; different pairs' test bodies may run at the same time as each other, bounded by an explicit concurrency limit (Build plan, step 1).

Happy path: `pnpm eval -t control-direct-match` scores that one pair for real, five sequential reruns under the one minted session, and prints a passing verdict with its denominator (e.g. "strong_match, 5 of 5 succeeded"), verifies **AC-1**, **AC-2**, **AC-6**, **AC-9**.

**Settled by spec 0017, accepted 2026-09-08**, and all three were decided: five reruns per pair, a `stability-probe` pair passing only when every rerun succeeds, and `tags` plus `acceptableBands` feeding a strict majority with a 3 of 5 floor, where `acceptableBands` is the exception applied when no majority forms.

The 3 of 5 success threshold for `inconclusive` means a genuinely bad but real result (all 5 reruns land on the same, wrong band) is never confused with a run too broken to trust, which is correct, but it also means an unlucky run (3 vendor timeouts and 2 real, matching answers) is reported exactly the same way as one with no useful data at all, even though 2 real matching answers is weak but real evidence. This spec accepts that loss rather than inventing a second, softer verdict tier.

Review it (fresh model): `/check review model client router` · two rounds, both reviewed on Claude Opus 5 against author Sonnet 5. **Round 1**, 2026-09-06, 21 files: verdict **Blocked**, one blocker (CI missing both new required env keys, `OPENAI_API_KEY` and `GOOGLE_GENERATIVE_AI_API_KEY`, which would have failed every check the moment a pull request opened), three majors and three minors. **Round 2**, 2026-09-06, a different Opus 5 instance, 24 files: independently re-verified all six round 1 findings rather than trusting the account (five resolved, one, the `withUsageGate` test mock, deliberately accepted), then found two new problems introduced by round 1's own fixes. Verdict **Changes requested**. Both new majors were fixed the same day, and one minor was taken (`truncated` registered as a queryable `ai.call_tier` span attribute in `spans.md`). **One round 2 minor was rejected on a false premise**: it claimed the three AI packages were the only floating runtime versions in `package.json`; counted directly, 19 of the repo's 30 dependencies use `^`, including `eslint`, `typescript`, `prettier` and every `@types/*`, and spec 0012's own Build plan step 1 says none pinned.

The thin thread: `test/eval/harness.test.ts`, one `describe("eval harness")`, a top level `beforeAll` running `validateGroundTruth()` (throwing with every issue if any, before anything else) then minting the one fixture session for the run; one `it.concurrent` per pair named `` `${pair.id} [${pair.tags.join(" ")}]` ``, whose body awaits five sequential `scoreListing()` calls, feeds the outcomes to step 2's verdict function, stores the result in a module scoped `Map<string, PairVerdict>` keyed by pair id, and asserts that the verdict's status is `pass`, so `fail` and `inconclusive` both fail their own test with the denominator and distribution in the message; and a final `afterAll` that runs the preference leak check against the map, writes the JSON report (including the model id and anchors hash), then deletes the fixture user. Prove this against exactly `control-direct-match` (real vendor calls) before scaling: get `pnpm eval -t control-direct-match` green end to end. Satisfies the first slice of **AC-1**, **AC-2**, **AC-9**.

The `weak_match` and `not_a_match` boundary is still undefined and is still recorded as a gap in spec [0016](../0016-eval-ground-truth-set/index.md)'s Follow up. **Three pairs sit on it, not two**, across thirty reruns: `key-domain-mismatch` (3 to 2, then 0 to 5), `weak-match-shallow-overlap` (4 to 1, then 3 to 2) and `boundary-seniority-gap` (`weak_match` 4 of 5 both runs, passing only through its widened tolerance). The one to watch is `weak-match-shallow-overlap`: it carries no tolerance and at 3 to 2 is a single rerun away from having no majority at all, so it is the pair most likely to fail next and the failure would be the boundary, not the pair. What would justify acting is repeated flipping, not one split.
A pair's five reruns are never fired concurrently with each other; only different pairs' test bodies may overlap (AC-2), bounded by `maxConcurrency` (Build plan, step 1).

**AC-9**: The command writes a JSON report every run, in addition to the console table, to a directory this repository does not track, at `test/eval/.output/<ISO timestamp with colons replaced by dashes>.json`, creating that directory if it does not exist. Each report is a single `EvalReport` object (defined in `test/eval/report.ts`) recording: the filter used (if any) and every skipped pair id; per pair, its status (`pass`/`fail`/`inconclusive`), sub reason where relevant, denominator, and every observed band (or band distribution); the preference leak check's own outcome; the run's overall status and aborted reason if any; and, once per report, which model answered (via the shared `resolvedModel()` guard on `TIERS.ai_scoring.model`, never a name typed into the harness) and a hash of `BAND_ANCHORS`'s current text (`bandAnchorsHash()`, defined once and shared with the AC-10 test, so "the same way" is true by construction rather than by two separate implementations agreeing).

**`skillCounts`** (added 2026-09-15, for the stopping rule in `## Follow-up`): computed by `refreshDemoResults()` from the rows it is about to write, never from a later read, as four numbers. `ownRoleRows` and `ownRoleEmpty` count the rows where the persona's own query kept the listing, up to 8, and how many of those carry an empty stored `matched_skills`. `crossRoleRows` and `crossRoleEmpty` count the same for the other rows. Both pairs are recorded on every completed run so the stopping rule is always read against the own role pair, never against all 16 rows.

If feature 16's eval harness later shows the five bands clustering rather than spreading (the condition **AC-2** defers to that harness), the band anchors in `rubric.ts` are the first thing to revise, not the vendor or any of this prompt's other instructions. **Still open, and its trigger has not fired.** Feature 16's harness ran the full sixteen pairs twice on 2026-09-08 and both runs observed all five bands, `strong_match` 35, `good_match` 5, `possible_match` 21, `weak_match` 11, `not_a_match` 8 in the first and 35, 4, 21, 8, 12 in the second, so the bands spread rather than clustered and AC-2's bar of at least three of five was already met. Spec 0018 did review the anchors, but for a different reason, two pairs disagreeing with their recorded expectation, and it concluded that `BAND_ANCHORS` holds and one committed expectation was wrong. No anchor changed and the hash is still `1b45f524b356`. So this item is neither satisfied nor superseded by that review; it is waiting on a clustering condition that has not been seen.

Export `resolvedModel()` from `src/lib/ai/tiers.ts`, and add `bandAnchorsHash()` as a small pure function in `src/features/scoring/eval/band-anchors-hash.ts`. Write the pure verdict logic in `test/helpers/eval-verdict.ts`: the three way outcome classification (refusal, rerun failure, scored success) from AC-3, the majority vote with the 3 of 5 inconclusive floor and the no majority/`acceptableBands` exception, the distinct `stability-probe` "every success inside `acceptableBands`" rule (AC-4), and the `preference-isolation` baseline comparison (AC-5). Wire `test/helpers/eval-verdict.test.ts` against constructed fixtures for each rule, no vendor call involved. Satisfies **AC-3**, **AC-4**, **AC-5**, **AC-6**.
**AC-3**: `scoreListing()` can return three kinds of outcome, and each is handled differently:

Verdict logic: the pure rerun outcome classification, majority vote with its no majority and `acceptableBands` exception, the `stability-probe` rule, and the `preference-isolation` baseline comparison, each proved against constructed fixtures with no vendor call, satisfies AC-3, AC-4, AC-5, AC-6.

Add the `eval` Vitest project to `vitest.config.mts`: `extends: true`, `include: ["test/eval/**/*.test.ts"]`, `environment: "node"`, the shared `setupFiles`, `globalSetup: ["./test/setup/require-stack.ts"]`, `testTimeout: 300_000`, `hookTimeout: 60_000`, `maxConcurrency: 4`, and `fileParallelism: false` scoped to this project alone. Add the `"eval": "vitest run --project eval"` script to `package.json`. Satisfies **AC-1**, **AC-2**, **AC-11**.

Scale to the full sixteen pairs, confirm `maxConcurrency` and `fileParallelism` behave as designed under a real, unfiltered `pnpm eval` run, and confirm the run's own exit code is non zero on a fail, an inconclusive pair, a leak, or an abort, and zero only when everything that ran passed cleanly. Satisfies the rest of **AC-1**, **AC-2**, **AC-7**, **AC-8**.

Project scaffolding: the `eval` Vitest project (`extends: true`, its own timeouts and `maxConcurrency`, `fileParallelism: false`), the `pnpm eval` script, and the shared `resolvedModel()`/`bandAnchorsHash()` helpers, satisfies AC-1, AC-2, AC-9, AC-11
The harness itself: the thin thread against one real pair, then the full sixteen with bounded concurrency and the run's own aggregate exit code, satisfies AC-1, AC-2, AC-7, AC-8, AC-9.

**AC-1**: One command (`pnpm eval`) runs every pair in feature 15's committed set and prints, for each pair, a pass, fail, or inconclusive verdict together with the actual band(s) observed. Before minting any session or spending any vendor call, a top level `beforeAll` runs `validateGroundTruth()` against the committed `ARCHETYPES` and `PAIRS`; if it returns any issue, the run throws with every issue printed, one per line, and exits non zero. This check runs even under a `-t` filtered invocation (AC-8),

Feature 16 (eval harness runner, not yet designed) needs to decide, as part of its own spec: how many times each pair reruns before a mismatch counts as a real regression rather than ordinary model noise (an earlier working note suggested 3 to 5 reruns per pair as a starting point); what counts as a pass for a `stability-probe` tagged pair (band variance across reruns, not a single match); and what each value in `tags` and the presence of `acceptableBands` should mean to its own pass or fail logic. This spec defines the data shape only, not the harness's interpretation of it.
Eval harness runner
Eval ground truth set

**Two bands now rest on a single pair each, not one.** Counting the committed set after this spec's correction: `strong_match` 7, `possible_match` 4, `not_a_match` 3, `good_match` 1, `weak_match` 1, sixteen pairs. `good-match-adjacent` holds the only exact `good_match` expectation, and `good_match` was already the thinnest observed band at 4 and 5 occurrences of 80. `weak-match-shallow-overlap` holds the only exact `weak_match` expectation. For either band, if its one pair moves, the band loses its exact expectation and `ground-truth.test.ts` names it, which is the guard working, but the set would want a second pair for that band before then. **`weak_match` is the more exposed of the two**, and the ground is this spec's own first Follow up item above: it puts `weak-match-shallow-overlap` on the still undefined `weak_match` and `not_a_match` boundary, records it moving 4 to 1 and then 3 to 2 across thirty reruns, and calls it the pair most likely to fail next. So the band with the thinner margin of safety is the one whose only holder this spec already predicts will move, while nothing similar is recorded against `good-match-adjacent`, which sat at `good_match` 4 of 5 in both runs.
Add `/test/eval/.output/` to `.gitignore`. Satisfies **AC-9**.

**AC-10**: A committed test (no vendor call, runs under the ordinary free unit suite) asserts `BAND_ANCHORS` literally equals today's text (`toEqual` against the five strings written inline in the test, never a snapshot file, which a routine `vitest -u` could silently rewrite) and that `bandAnchorsHash(BAND_ANCHORS)` equals today's computed hash, both failing by name and naming spec 0016's dataset, the moment either changes,

**AC-11**: The command works against a changed model with no code edit to this feature: nothing here names a vendor or a model id directly, every call goes through the existing `scoreListing()` / `TIERS` path exactly as the rest of the app does, and the model id reported (AC-9) is read off that same resolved config.

Failure case: a pair whose five reruns come back as 2 scored and 3 vendor failures is reported `inconclusive` (`insufficient-successes`) rather than a false pass or fail, the run's own exit code is non zero, and the other pairs in the same run still complete, verifies **AC-3**, **AC-7**.

Abort case: constructed against `test/helpers/eval-verdict.test.ts`'s own fixtures, the first rerun outcome carrying `allowed: false` (any `UsageGateReason`) stops the run from counting it toward any denominator and marks the run `aborted`, verifies **AC-3**.

**AC-5**: The three `preference-isolation` tagged pairs (`preference-match`, `preference-violation`, `preference-title-conflict`) are each judged individually by AC-3 first, exactly like any other pair, with no special treatment of their own verdicts. Once all three have a verdict that is neither `inconclusive` nor missing (skipped by a `-t` filter that excluded one of them, in which case the check below is skipped and reported as `leak-check-skipped`), the run additionally compares `preference-match`'s verdict band against `preference-violation`'s and against `preference-title-conflict`'s:

**AC-7**: The command's own exit code is non zero if any pair fails, any pair is `inconclusive`, a preference leak is reported, or the run aborted on a usage gate refusal (AC-3); zero only when every pair that ran passed cleanly and nothing aborted.

**AC-8**: A subset of pairs can be run without spending calls on the rest of the set, by reusing the test runner's own name filter against each pair's test name, which is generated as `` `${pair.id} [${pair.tags.join(" ")}]` `` (e.g. `control-direct-match [control]`, `stability-probe-generic [stability-probe]`), so `pnpm eval -t control-direct-match` matches one pair by id and `pnpm eval -t stability-probe` matches every pair carrying that tag. A filtered run still writes a JSON report; it records which filter produced it and lists every pair that did not run as `skipped`, never silently absent. Filters can overlap (e.g. `-t control` also matches every pair whose id happens to start with `control-`); this is an accepted property of substring matching, not a bug to design around.
Data quality gate: `validateGroundTruth()` returning even one issue against a deliberately broken fixture set stops the command before any vendor call is made, verifies **AC-1**.

**Should `control-one-gap` keep its `control` tag?** This pair no longer behaves that way: `possible_match` won it 4 to 1, then 5 to 0, then 3 to 2 on the confirming run, so it now passes on the narrowest majority the harness accepts. Spec [0016](../0016-eval-ground-truth-set/index.md) draws this exact distinction when it explains why `mild-stretch-possible-match` carries "no `acceptableBands` and the plain `control` tag rather than `boundary`": the tag tracks whether the anchor text settles the pair, not how the model happens to answer. **Recorded here, not answered.** Whoever takes it up should know the two obvious moves are both constrained: retagging it `boundary` would concede that the anchors do not settle it, which contradicts this spec's own finding that they do, and widening it with `acceptableBands` is refused outright by the Key invariants above. `ground-truth.test.ts` now asserts that no `control` tagged pair carries `acceptableBands`, so the retag and the tolerance are not independent choices.

**AC-4b**: Spec 0016's two now stale references to `control-one-gap` are corrected: its table row at line 141 lists the pair as `good_match`, and its Follow up at line 182 quotes that pair's rationale saying "That is good_match's wording" as present tense evidence of how the set was authored. The row is updated and the Follow up quote is marked as historical, true of the set as authored and superseded here. Both are recording edits, not changes to what spec 0016 decides.

**A v2 consideration, not v1 or v1.5: JobsPipe (https://jobspipe.dev) as an alternative to the approach above, not an addition to it.** It would remove the need for a second request and any HTML parsing, Verified 2026-09-08 against their OpenAPI spec (jobspipe.dev/openapi.json) and terms page, the `Job` schema's `description` field reads "Full text of the posting as published by the source", against Adzuna's 500 character excerpt; it also returns `seniority`, `work_arrangement` (remote/hybrid/onsite), `status` (active/closed), `keyword_slugs`, `min/max_annual_salary_usd`, and `discovered_at` for incremental polling; credits are 1 per job returned, `blur_company_data=true` returns rows for zero credits, the free tier is 1,000 jobs a month with `limit` capped at 25 (about 50 searches a month at 20 listings each, against the current cap of roughly 108), and the first paid tier is $49 a month for 25,000; their terms state no attribution requirement, which would make spec 0013's AC-6 and AC-7 apparatus (the attribution component, the logo geometry, the mandated link targets) deletable rather than portable; their terms do **not** address caching or storage, a gap rather than a permission, and this app stores listing fields on `application` rows, so that has to be resolved with the vendor in writing before anyone relies on it. Two other places already point at this same decision, so treat it as one rather than three: `docs/feature-14-v2-architecture.md`'s extract-then-score pipeline names full posting text as its own unmet precondition and is not referenced anywhere else in this scope; and spec 0016's Consequences already names the switching cost, that feature 15's sixteen ground truth pairs stop matching what the model sees the moment full postings arrive and need a deliberate re-authoring pass.

**Done by spec 0017's AC-10**, and by the concrete way this item names: `src/features/scoring/eval/band-anchors.test.ts` pins the anchor wording, and its failure message names this dataset and `pairs.ts` by path, telling the reader to re-argue each affected pair rather than update the expectation. A second assertion pins `bandAnchorsHash(BAND_ANCHORS)`, which is the value written into every eval report, so a change to the hash function alone is caught as well. It runs in the free unit suite, so drift is caught by `pnpm test`.

Add the committed `BAND_ANCHORS` drift test under `src/features/scoring/eval/` (the ordinary unit project, no vendor call): a literal `toEqual` pin of today's text plus a `bandAnchorsHash()` equality check, both failing by name, pointing at spec 0016's dataset, the moment either changes. Satisfies **AC-10**.
Drift guard: editing `BAND_ANCHORS`'s text fails the AC-10 test by name, under the ordinary free `pnpm test`, verifies **AC-10**.
The drift guard: the committed `BAND_ANCHORS` snapshot test under the free unit suite, and the gitignored output directory, satisfies AC-10.

claims.text: Spec 0018 says the `5 of 5` in a `summary` like "possible_match, 5 of 5 succeeded" is the success denominator, meaning all five reruns returned a band. It is not the count landing on that band, so it cannot show how the reruns split.
Spec 0018 therefore tells readers to use `distribution`, never `summary`, when the question is how the reruns split.

This does not contradict spec 0017's AC-6, which requires every verdict to name its denominator, such as "good_match, 3 of 3 succeeded", never just a band. That denominator is the count of successful reruns, not a per-band count.

Spec 0017 reports a distribution-shaped verdict as a per-band split with the denominator, e.g. "3 strong_match / 2 possible_match, 5 of 5 succeeded". A stability-probe pair is always reported as its observed distribution, never a lone band. So the per-band split lives in the distribution, and the denominator only says how many reruns were scored.
